Bay Area heat advisory extended through Wednesday as mid-90s temperatures bake 49ers game
As a sweltering October heat wave drives fans to searing temperatures at Levi's Stadium, residents across the region scramble to alter routines, hydrate and beat the smog.
If Bay Area residents thought the weekend was hot, brace for it. The National Weather Service has extended a heat advisory for most of the region to last at least through Wednesday.
The intense temperatures have forced residents to pivot their plans, while thousands of football fans gear up to watch the 49ers during a very hot midday game.
Game time is set for 1:25 p.m. Sunday, when temperatures are expected to reach the mid-90s. Fans attending the matchup against the Broncos must contend with the stadium's layout.
"The way the stadium is designed, people on the west side of the stadium, the sun is crazy," said Ulises Moreno of Campbell, noting that an entire section of Levi's Stadium sits right smack in the sun.
While Levi's Stadium may look cool and inviting at night, fans who plan to be there know they may be sizzling.
The sweltering conditions also emptied public spaces across the region. In Campbell, a basketball court that is usually packed was almost deserted. Even those who braved the heat to practice admitted it was taking a toll.
"I'm getting a headache from the heat, but I still wanna get my shots up," said Giovvani Gomez of San Jose, who hoped hydration would help him push through.
Local
Pet owners adjusted their routines as well. Bretton Paul opted to wait until temperatures dropped into the 80s to take his dog, Roxy, for a walk, taking extra precautions to keep his four-legged friend safe.
"We have booties that we put on her when it's extra hot on the asphalt, and we also give her lots of water, and we don't go out when it's too hot," Paul said.
"It's hot, hot, hot," said Roberto Gomez of San Jose. "I had to get out of the house and get around. It's been hot all day."
While the intense temperatures are expected to last until Wednesday, residents found a few silver linings, enjoying fall al fresco dining, nighttime water playtime, and open-air cruising.
However, the heat wave brings environmental concerns alongside the sunshine. NBC's Marianne Favro reported live from Santa Clara that another Spare the Air day is expected due to elevated concentrations of smog.
"If you're truly a faithful fan, you'll deal with triple-digit temps and bad air," one 49ers fan told Favro.
